text: Replace pointwise BCE with a within-user listwise softmax loss: for each training user having both positive and negative impressions, normalize exponentiated scores across that user's impressions and minimize cross-entropy against the user's normalized long_view labels; retain the factorization-machine architecture, request-context features, split, checkpointing protocol, and fixed evaluation unchanged.
rationale: This directly targets the official mean of within-user GAUC and nDCG@5 without changing the ranking evaluator, and is distinct from the recently attempted sampled BPR objective. The reference model reached primary 0.602935, GAUC 0.668912, and nDCG@5 0.536958, while top-five diagnostics remained limited (Precision@5 0.375364, MAP@5 0.485656, MRR@5 0.542483, Recall@5 0.600268, HitRate@5 0.677258). Classification remains recall-heavy (0.758995 recall versus 0.483470 precision and 0.630064 specificity; Matthews correlation 0.360963), suggesting score separation and calibration are not fully aligned with within-user ordering. Train only on mixed-label users, exclude all-positive and all-negative groups from the listwise loss, and verify finite scores plus stable data diagnostics (positive rate 0.313284, score mean -0.980009, score standard deviation 1.408575). Accept only if primary improves over the reference while monitoring GAUC, nDCG@5, classification, ranking, and segment diagnostics.
